gallery.title: File:Istanbul Rahmi M Koc Museum 5998.jpg
gallery.description: Horse tram. Horse trams, which were accepted as the most advanced means of mass road transportation of their time, were inspired from vehicles used in mines to carry coal in England. The first example of a horse tram was seen in New York in 1832 and later they began to be used in Europe. The horse tram made its first trip in Turkey on September 3rd 1872. […] In Turkey, horse trams were replaced by electrical ones in 1914. The one shown here worked route 14 between Beşiktaş and Karaköy and is shown in its original Ottoman livery.

gallery.filename: Istanbul Rahmi M. Koç Museum “Tünel” Carriage and railway winding engine 2015 6028.jpg
gallery.title: File:Istanbul Rahmi M. Koç Museum “Tünel” Carriage and railway winding engine 2015 6028.jpg
gallery.source: Istanbul Rahmi M. Koç Museum “Tünel” Carriage and railway winding engine 2015 6028
gallery.description: “Tünel” Carriage and railway winding engine. The “Tünel” – a short, steep underground railway from Galata up to Istiklal Street – was opened for service on the 17th of January 1875 and is the third oldest passenger underground, after London and New York. This original wagon was initially hauled on a metal strap by massive steam engines, one of which is also exhibited alongside, a magnificent horizontal duplex steam engine made by the Schneider-Creusot iron and steel works in France in 1873.
